newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil matches IPE gains, diesel jumps again.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil matches IPE gains, diesel jumps again.

text.p: NWE gas oil rose on Monday, supported by sharp gains in November IPE futures and continuing shortages of low sulphur diesel, traders said.
Early gains on IPE futures were swollen by a U.S. refinery fire, renewing fears of tight supplies of heating oil ahead of winter. Nov IPE closed $7.50 higher at $234.00 a tonne.
Premiums over the November screen for diesel rose towards $40 per tonne as refiners, especially in Germany and France, scrambled for product.
One German major bought 20,000 tonnes at what he said was in the area of Nov IPE +$35/38 cif Hamburg.
He said he did not want to disclose the exact price because it was "too painful. I paid a hell of a lot too many dollars."
Heating oil cargo premiums were steady at Nov IPE +$10-12 cif Hamburg, and traders differed over whether this market was oversupplied.
One saw large volumes available from the U.S. but this was of variable quality and much of it did not meet German specifications.
Barge market premiums also held steady around Nov IPE +$5/7 fob ARA.
